articles.title: DeepSeek Harness不可错过的12款神器！还有崔添翼推荐的
articles.text:
智东西
作者 | 江宇
编辑 | 漠影
一批民间开源插件正涌入DeepSeek Harness。
智东西10月21日报道，截至今日，DeepSeek Harness在全球开发者平台GitHub上已经拿下超过25万Stars。开源短短两个多月，DeepSeek Harness已经吸引一批开发者为它打造插件，相关开源项目不断涌现。
为此，我们从GitHub、X、Reddit等平台搜罗了一批DeepSeek Harness第三方插件及适配项目，综合参考项目在GitHub上的Star数，以及其在X、Reddit等社区获得的关注度和业内知名开发者的推荐情况，从中筛选出12个值得关注的项目。
这批项目里，有的已经在GitHub上拿下数万甚至超过10万Stars，有的获得了现任DeepSeek产品部负责人、DeepSeek Harness团队负责人崔添翼的关注和推荐。
还有一些小工具，专门解决具体问题：让纯文本模型看懂截图，让长任务在上下文压缩后接着跑，或者直接在对话里修改简历。
其中，开源设计工具OpenDesign的主仓库Star数已达到10.28万；侧边栏增强插件DSH Better Sidebar获得约4400 Stars，上下文管理插件dsh-context获得约2700 Stars，这两款插件均获得了崔添翼的关注和推荐。
这些项目的用途五花八门。
有的将文件管理、代码编辑和Git操作集中到一个侧边栏，有的专门盯着Agent的Token消耗，还有的能让DeepSeek Harness操作浏览器、跨会话找回之前的信息。
开发者们各自瞄准一个使用痛点，给DeepSeek Harness补上自己想要的功能。
围绕插件生态，DeepSeek Harness团队此前称，其将持续支持第三方插件生态的发展，改善第三方插件的发现、获取和管理体验，并建设官方插件市场。
目前，DeepSeek Harness已经提供实验性的自定义插件市场功能。用户启用后，可以在插件页面的“发现”（Discover）标签中添加第三方索引，浏览和安装插件。
在官方插件市场进一步完善之前，社区开发者已经各显神通。下面，我们就来看看，这些“为爱发电”的民间项目到底有什么惊喜。
一、工作台大改造！侧边栏、上下文、插件市场都有人操心
先来看更贴近日常使用的一类插件。聊天时想顺手查看文件，运行Agent时想知道上下文还剩多少，安装新插件时又得四处找GitHub地址……这些看似琐碎的需求，都有社区开发者专门做了工具来解决。
1、DSH Better Sidebar：崔添翼推荐，给DeepSeek Harness装上增强版侧边栏
https://github.com/omdsh-dev/DSH-better-sidebar
DSH Better Sidebar是一款界面增强插件，它把文件管理、代码编辑、终端操作、Git管理以及子Agent信息整合到了侧边栏和底部工作台中。
例如，用户让DeepSeek Harness修改代码后，可以直接在侧边栏查看文件、检查改动，必要时再打开终端操作，不用在编辑器、终端和DeepSeek Harness之间反复切换。
这款插件还提供扩展接口，其他开发者可以在其基础上添加新的侧边栏页面或文件预览器。
9月27日，崔添翼曾在X上专门分享这款插件，介绍它如何利用DeepSeek Harness原生界面能力扩展工作台。
值得注意的是，这款插件与DeepSeek Harness宿主版本存在对应关系，安装时需要选择匹配的插件版本。
2、dsh-context：把Agent的上下文消耗摊开给你看
https://github.com/bowenliang123/dsh-context
dsh-context可以让用户看清楚，Agent到底把上下文用在了哪里。它提供上下文可视化面板，可以查看当前会话占用了多少Token、系统提示词和工具结果各占多少比例，以及上下文如何随着任务推进不断增长。
当Agent运行时间较长、回答质量出现波动时，用户可以通过图表检查上下文组成，查看是否发生了压缩等事件。它还支持跨会话统计、Token和费用估算，以及多Agent使用情况展示。
▲The Context Insights page
崔添翼等DeepSeek Harness团队成员曾推荐这款插件，并为项目点Star。
3、dsh-market：民间开发者自己搭了一个插件商店
https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market
有了越来越多的第三方插件，去哪找、怎么装，就成了新的麻烦。dsh-market把插件市场直接搬进DeepSeek Harness，支持按名称、功能和类别搜索插件，查看插件介绍，并在界面中完成安装和管理。
它还提供主题管理、收藏等功能，让用户寻找插件时不必每次都去GitHub搜索。
随着DeepSeek Harness新版加入实验性的Discover功能，dsh-market也提供了兼容的市场索引。用户可以把其社区插件目录接入DeepSeek Harness原生发现页面。
不过，社区市场收录并不等于官方质量认证，安装前仍需核对插件来源。
4、DSH Desktop：桌面客户端也有人重新造了一遍
https://github.com/anywhere-labs/dsh-desktop
除了给界面添加功能，还有开发者索性自己做了一套桌面客户端。DSH Desktop是一款由社区独立开发的桌面客户端项目，围绕DeepSeek Harness运行时提供桌面窗口、终端集成及插件管理等功能。
这款客户端同样采用可组合的插件架构，开发者可以根据自己的需求调整界面、增加功能，把DeepSeek Harness改造成自己习惯的工作环境。
目前，DeepSeek也已经提供官方DeepSeek Harness桌面版。DSH Desktop属于独立社区项目，其兼容性取决于客户端所搭载的DeepSeek Harness运行时版本。
二、给Agent补上眼睛和双手！看图、搜索、操作浏览器
如果说前面几款插件主要在改造DeepSeek Harness的使用界面，接下来这三款则直接给Agent增加了新本领。看不懂图片，就接入视觉引擎；没法联网，就补上搜索工具；需要操作网页，还有插件能替它点击和填写表单。
5、ModLens：给纯文本模型外挂一双“眼睛”
https://github.com/liustack/modlens
当用户发来一张界面截图，底层模型却无法直接理解图片时，该怎么办？ModLens提供了一种解决办法：通过外部视觉引擎分析图片，再把OCR识别结果、页面布局和图像语义等信息转换成结构化数据，供Agent使用。
例如，开发者可以向DeepSeek Harness提供一张网页设计截图，让视觉服务识别其中的文字和界面结构，再交给Agent参考。
这款插件主要面向视觉能力不足或仅支持文本输入的模型，但需要配置相应视觉API或CLI服务，具体成本取决于所使用的视觉提供方。
6、ModSearch：给DeepSeek Harness补上联网搜索能力
https://github.com/liustack/modsearch
ModSearch解决的是另一个常见问题：当底层模型不能联网时，怎样让它获取网上的实时信息？这款插件支持网页搜索、页面内容抓取，并能把搜索结果整理成带有来源信息的结构化数据。
它可以连接Firecrawl、Keenable、Tavily、Exa等搜索服务，部分默认通道提供免密钥额度。
例如，用户让DeepSeek Harness搜集某个开源项目的最新资料，插件可以帮助Agent搜索相关页面、读取网页内容，再将获取的信息交给模型处理，省去人工逐个复制网页内容的步骤。
ModSearch还支持X平台搜索，但相关能力需要配合Grok Build使用，并非所有搜索通道都免费、免登录。
7、dsh-browser：让DeepSeek Harness直接操作浏览器
https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-browser
如果用户查完资料，还想让Agent帮忙点击网页、填写表单，dsh-browser就能派上用场。它提供了Chrome扩展与DeepSeek Harness插件的组合方案，让Agent通过浏览器页面结构执行导航、点击、输入等操作。
例如，用户可以让DeepSeek Harness进入一个网页，查找指定位置的信息，再根据任务要求进行后续操作。这款插件主要依靠页面结构获取元素信息，无需每次都把网页转换成截图，再交给视觉模型识别。
当然，网页操作涉及授权和隐私。插件对受浏览器保护的页面存在访问限制，用户也需要谨慎设置操作权限。
三、Agent干活别再“失忆”！长任务和跨会话记忆也有外挂
长任务最怕干到一半，Agent把前面的事情给忘了。上下文被压缩、会话被清空，用户又得重新交代背景和进度。
针对这个问题，社区开发者给出了两种方案：一种把计划和进度存进文件，另一种直接给Agent接入记忆系统。
8、Planning with Files：把任务计划写下来，断了还能接着干
https://github.com/OthmanAdi/planning-with-files
Planning with Files是一套面向长任务的文件化规划方案，目前已经适配多种AI编程Agent，并提供DeepSeek Harness专用插件。它会将任务计划、研究发现和执行进度保存到文件中，使Agent能够在后续执行时重新读取这些信息。
比如，用户让DeepSeek Harness开发一个网站，涉及页面设计、接口开发和测试等多个环节。通过这套方案，Agent可以持续记录任务完成情况，在会话中断或上下文压缩后，再依据文件恢复进度。项目还提供任务状态检查等功能，帮助Agent判断各个阶段是否真正完成。
这样一来，用户就不用在每次重新开启任务时，都从头向Agent解释哪些工作已经做完、接下来还要做什么。
9、OpenViking：接入4万Stars记忆系统，帮Agent找回往事
https://github.com/volcengine/OpenViking
Planning with Files主要负责保存任务计划，而OpenViking进一步瞄准了Agent的记忆问题。OpenViking由火山引擎开源，是一套面向Agent的上下文与记忆管理系统，提供记忆、知识检索和Skills管理能力。
它已经提供DeepSeek Harness专用记忆插件，可以记录会话信息，在后续任务中检索并召回相关内容。
例如，用户之前向Agent交代过一个项目的技术背景，再次打开新会话时，记忆系统可以帮助Agent找回相关资料，减少重复输入。
不过，OpenViking的接入门槛相对更高，除了安装DeepSeek Harness插件，还需要配置能够访问的OpenViking服务。
四、10万Stars项目也来了！设计、简历、编程都有专用方案
还有一批开发者，直接把已经成熟的开源工具接进DeepSeek Harness。这些工具有的已经积累数万Stars，原本就有自己的产品和用户群。通过适配DeepSeek Harness，它们又多了一种由AI Agent参与操作的方式。
10、OpenDesign：超10万Stars的AI设计工作台
https://github.com/nexu-io/open-design
这是本次盘点中GitHub热度最高的项目。OpenDesign是一款开源AI设计工作台，支持制作网页、交互原型、应用界面、仪表盘和演示文稿等内容。
用户可以在工作台中提出设计需求，结合AI Agent生成和修改作品，并通过可视化界面继续调整。
OpenDesign支持连接多种编程Agent，其中就包括DeepSeek Harness。根据项目接入文档，它能够调用用户已安装的DeepSeek Harness，并通过专门的运行时适配组件进行通信，让DeepSeek Harness参与设计工作流。
11、Reactive Resume：4万多Stars的简历工具，让Agent来帮忙
https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume
在一众面向程序员的插件中，Reactive Resume算是一个比较接地气的项目。它原本是一款开源简历制作工具，支持简历创建、编辑和管理。现在，项目提供了专用DeepSeek Harness插件，通过MCP服务将简历管理能力接入Agent。
用户可以直接在DeepSeek Harness对话中读取已有简历、创建新简历或修改简历内容，不用每次都自己打开简历编辑界面逐项调整。
比如，用户想针对一个岗位修改项目经历，就可以让Agent读取简历内容，根据要求调整相关描述，再通过工具接口保存修改结果。
这一方案需要配置Reactive Resume的API密钥，具体操作能力也取决于其服务接口。
12、DeepSeek Reasonix：把另一个编程Agent招来当帮手
https://github.com/esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix
最后这款项目主要面向有复杂开发需求的用户。DeepSeek Reasonix是一款独立的AI编程Agent，支持处理软件工程任务。
其开发者提供了DeepSeek Harness接入方案，通过Agent Client Protocol（ACP）协议，让Reasonix以子Agent的形式接受DeepSeek Harness分配的任务。
例如，DeepSeek Harness在处理一个较复杂的软件项目时，可以把其中一部分编程任务交给Reasonix执行，再接收其返回的结果。
该方案已针对DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-rc.2进行验证。接入时需要预先安装Reasonix、配置模型服务，并使用与DeepSeek Harness宿主版本匹配的ACP组件。
结语：民间插件越做越多，怎么管理成了新问题
这12个项目只是DeepSeek Harness第三方生态的一部分。插件多了之后，新的麻烦也随之出现。
DeepSeek Harness本身还在持续迭代，部分插件可能因为宿主版本升级而无法正常运行。不同插件的安装方式、依赖环境和权限要求也不一样，用户找到了想用的功能，未必就能顺利装上。尤其是能够读取本地文件、执行命令或操作浏览器的插件，还涉及权限和安全问题。
目前，DeepSeek Harness已经推出实验性的插件发现机制。接下来，官方插件市场如何建设，能否让用户更方便地找到兼容、可信的插件，值得继续关注。
从目前这批项目来看，DeepSeek Harness的“一切皆插件”，已经吸引了一批社区开发者动手实践。

articles.title: The Download: introducing the Impossible issue
articles.text:
This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.
Introducing: the Impossible issue
We wanted our last print edition of 2026 to include a slate of stories that check in on impossible ideas. Why? Because it’s fun to dream about living on other planets or uploading our brains. But also because scientists and engineers who won’t give up on daring endeavors remind us what technology is supposed to do: make life better, safer, healthier, even more joyful.
That’s the ambition behind the stories in our new Impossible issue. We explore bold attempts to make synthetic blood, build cities on the moon, and attain cognitive immortality. We investigate AI’s ability to say no, a bionic eye that can restore sight, and high hopes for blended meat. Plus, we check in on six technologies that have been “coming soon” for years.
This issue is for the folks with the audacity to try, and refuse to let anyone—themselves included— tell them no. We hope you enjoy the ride.
Subscribe now to read the full print issue.
Astrolab’s upcoming rover will run the first LLMs on the moon
Large language models are set to go lunar. A computer capable of running AI software is one of the payloads aboard Astrolab’s FLIP lunar rover, which is slated to head to the moon as early as next month.
The mission will test whether LLMs can enable greater autonomy and real-time intelligent decision-making in the extreme lunar environment. But the moon will present formidable challenges, from extreme temperatures to intense cosmic radiation.
Find out how the lunar rover could change the future of space exploration.
—Tereza Pultarova
How to study a swiftly melting climate disaster
In Alaska’s Denali National Park, a 2013 lightning fire burned nearly 35,000 acres, stripping away the insulating layer that preserves permafrost. It’s given scientists a rare opportunity to study how fires reshape permafrost and carbon storage over time.
The work is providing critical clues into the complex mechanisms driving cascading climate feedback effects. As warming temperatures fuel fires, more permafrost thaws, releasing greenhouse-gas emissions that threaten to fuel more warming, fires and permafrost loss. Their observations are revealing worrisome signs about what lies ahead.
Discover what their fieldwork is revealing about a cascading climate disaster.
—James Temple
MIT Technology Review Narrated: the explosive claim that’s upended the AI world
“I think I have good news about the nature of neural networks.” With those simple words of optimism, Nick Cammarata, a researcher at AI startup Goodfire, kicked off a 26,000-word blog post that has knocked the industry on its head.
Cammarata claims that LLMs might be far easier to understand, and thus to monitor and control, than people previously thought. If true, it’s a huge deal. But not everyone is convinced.
MIT Technology Review spoke to Cammarata the day after his post blew up. He explained what he thinks researchers are getting wrong, what his work actually shows, and why skeptics aren’t ready to celebrate just yet.
This is our latest story to become an MIT Technology Review Narrated podcast, which we publish each week on Spotify and Apple Podcasts. Just navigate to MIT Technology Review Narrated on either platform, and follow us to get all our new content as it’s released.
The must-reads
I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.
1 Elon Musk reportedly ordered the recent Starlink slowdown in Ukraine
The restrictions hampered drone strikes and air defences. (WSJ $)
+ The move sparked confusion in Washington over who authorised it. (CNBC)
+ Ukraine’s volunteer army is keeping Starlink alive. (MIT Technology Review)
2 An OpenAI model disabled its own safety checks—then lied about it
Two agents weakened the company’s safeguards during routine tasks. (CNBC)
+ They turned off systems designed to spot their misbehaviour. (FT $)
+ Here’s why AI agents lie to reach their goals. (MIT Technology Review)
3 SpaceX and Tesla have begun merger discussions
They’ve formed special committees to discuss a deal. (BBC)
+ Elon Musk, the CEO of both companies, said it’s “a good idea.” (Axios)
+ A merger could combine their AI and manufacturing plans. (Reuters $)
4 Global emissions have stalled, but warming is heading towards 2.8°C
The UN says the 1.5°C climate target is now out of reach. (Nature)
+ Current pledges would still bring warming to 2.1°C. (New Scientist $)
+ Climate tech companies offer rays of hope. (MIT Technology Review)
5 Ukraine says it’s carried out the world’s first drone evacuation
A heavy hexacopter flew a soldier to safety. (Ars Technica)
+ Ukraine has shared a video showing the evacuation. (CNBC)
+ A Russian satellite recently stalked a spacecraft believed to support Ukraine. (NYT $)
6 Meta has paused Muse sharing after private chats surfaced online
Researchers found 6,800 links exposing sensitive conversations. (Verge)
+ AI agents are not your “coworkers.” (MIT Technology Review)
7 More than 1,000 mathematicians have pledged to shun AI companies
Some also vowed to avoid AI tools in their research. (New Scientist $)
8 AI is making it easy to clone almost any software
Viral tools promise easy copying, but often produce slop. (404 Media)
9 A computer program has finally outdone humans at cryptic crosswords
Its creator hopes to tackle the harder challenge of setting puzzles. (Guardian)
10 A newly-discovered particle could explain the origins of reality
In particular, it could reveal why matter survived the Big Bang. (404 Media)
Quote of the day
“I did not remove an enabled monitor from it.”
—GPT-6 Astra, an OpenAI coding agent, tells its user it hasn’t disabled a safeguard after doing exactly that, the company reveals in a new misalignment report.
One more thing
This giant microwave may change the future of war
US armed forces are hunting for a weapon that disables drones en masse—and they want it fast.
One solution focuses on microwaves: high-powered electronic devices that push out kilowatts of power to zap the circuits of a drone as if it were the tinfoil you forgot to take off your leftovers when you heated them up.
Defense tech startup Epirus may have the winning formula. The company has developed a cutting-edge, cost-efficient drone zapper that’s sparking the interest of the US military—and drones are just one of its targets. Peer into its crosshairs.
—Sam Dean
We can still have nice things
A place for comfort, fun, and distraction to brighten up your day. (Got any ideas? Drop me a line.)
+ Don’t feel guilty about enjoying a siesta; fish take naps during the day, too.
+ Every trade has its go-to tools. This site has built a fascinating register of them.
+ Wikipop spotlights what was most popular on Wikipedia yesterday, providing a daily snapshot of what the world is reading.
+ Meet the self-taught woodcarver who went from a broke young father to creating some of Disneyland’s most iconic attractions.

articles.title: GTC Berlin 2026: Live Updates From NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang’s Keynote
articles.text:
Founded in a tent near the Berlin Wall in 1980, the Tempodrom moved several times before settling near Anhalter Bahnhof in 2001. Its permanent home has since hosted concerts, galas and political events.
Today, it hosts a different kind of spectacle.
GTC Berlin runs three days, with more than 100 sessions on agentic AI, robotics, physical AI, open models and accelerated computing underway at STATION-Berlin down the road. Here, journalists, analysts and partners have gathered for the main event: NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang’s keynote.
Huang Takes the Stage
Huang opened with a question: What do L’Oréal, Revolut, Spotify, Merck, Vodafone, Zara, Porsche, Nestlé and HSBC have in common? They’re all European companies and they’re all working with NVIDIA on AI, he said.
The keynote comes on the heels of NVIDIA’s weeklong road across Europe — Paris, London, Stockholm, Dublin — with the company committing nearly $10 billion to the technology ecosystem across Europe and working with 12,000+ partners. “After decades of advancement in the computer industry, we are now at the beginnings of a new industrial revolution,” Huang said.
Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements
AI is a five-layer cake, Huang explained. Energy powers advanced computers that are part of an AI factory, which generates tokens and digital intelligence from the models that run on it, which are then integrated into every application.
“Long before the AI models emerge, the infrastructure has to exist,” he said, highlighting how, similarly, the internet first needed networking, and electricity first required the grid.
“To be part of this AI economy, you don’t want to just be consuming the AI; you want to be producing the AI,” Huang said. “We could do all of that here in Europe, and in fact, we’ve already started.”
The AI Factory Gets a New Form Factor
Huang framed NVIDIA’s full-stack AI factory — spanning hardware, system software, CUDA-X libraries and models — as a broad platform for building and operating AI infrastructure.
“This now represents the breadth of technology necessary to create the AI factory,” Huang said. “This is what NVIDIA builds today, and this is the foundation by which we can enable Europe to be part of the AI ecosystem, the AI economy.”
He said Vera Rubin, in full production, extends NVIDIA’s computing platform beyond models and large language models to process the entire AI agent. He also showed several of NVIDIA’s latest rack-scale hardware offerings.
Next, Huang announced NVIDIA DSX POD, a reference design for complete NVIDIA Vera Rubin AI factories built by partners inside modular containers, integrated and validated before delivery. With DSX POD, onsite deployment can shrink from six months to just 14 days once site utilities are ready.
“This is a complete transformation of the world supply chain,” Huang said. “This will change the way that people install and build data centers, and hopefully, as a result, velocity goes up.”
The NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform enables companies to reduce water consumption for cooling by up to 100% and generate the same AI output with up to 30% less power.
Agents Are the New Computing Platform — and Safety Is an Engineering Problem
Huang said agents think, reason, iterate and use tools, driving token consumption as they become more useful.
He described an agent as comprising five elements: a model, a harness that orchestrates its work and memory, a sandbox that isolates the harness, knowledge and tools. In that framing, an agent is more than a model answering questions; it can draw on knowledge and act through tools.
“The most important thing is to make sure the agent is secure,” Huang said. The autonomous agent can access files, resources, networks and tools, so its privileges should be minimal and it should be monitored.
NVIDIA’s answer is the new NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture for Safe AI Agents, a full-stack design built on NVIDIA OpenShell — an open source, policy-controlled runtime with kernel-level sandboxing that sits between an agent and the systems it can affect.
That means privileges, policy enforcement and monitoring must adapt dynamically. “Every single time an agent is launched, the privileges are different,” Huang said.
Open Models Turn Expertise Into an Advantage
Huang presented NVIDIA’s open models as a starting point for building AI tailored to specific needs.
NVIDIA’s frontier, open models are available for use across industries: Nemotron for language, Cosmos for world foundation models, GR00T for humanoid robotics, Alpamayo for autonomous vehicles, Ising for quantum-classical computing and Earth-2 for physics AI.
“We are the frontier,” Huang said. “So in all of these different areas, we offer you all of the models, and we’re continuously working on it. We’ve been working on it for a decade, and we’ll continue to work on this forever.”
NVIDIA provides the models, data and scripts to reproduce them, and companies can post-train a model on their own data for a particular use case — turning proprietary data into what he called “sovereign intelligence.”
“You could start with an open model, something that’s incredibly good like Nemotron, and with your own data, post-train it for your use case and achieve, of course, super intelligence,” Huang said. “That is a very sensible thing to do, and all the technology exists today.”
NVIDIA Gives Agents a Knowledge Layer
Huang then introduced the NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation as a set of models and libraries for connecting agents to enterprise data, whether it’s unstructured information in documents or structured data in databases.
He highlighted Nemotron tools for parsing documents, embedding queries and reranking relevant information, along with new NVIDIA Kumo models for making predictions from structured data.
“Ultimately, what turns these super agents, these agents into super agents, is that you give them access to your company’s knowledge,” Huang said.
NVIDIA CUDA-X — Accelerated Tools for Agents
Huang then described NVIDIA CUDA-X as a collection of accelerated libraries used across science, engineering, research and creative work.
NVIDIA’s accelerated computing platform has more than 11 million developers building on it.
Huang said those libraries can accelerate simulators, solvers and data-processing engines — the kinds of tools agents may draw on to do useful work.
“CUDA-X tools are what gives agents the tools of the trade,” Huang said.
Agents Go to Work in Labs, Factories and Engineering
A video showcased NVIDIA Agent Toolkit bringing company knowledge, models and tools together in three industry examples:
At Lila Sciences, agents help design a potential B-cell lymphoma therapy, using virtual experiments to guide work in an automated lab.
At Siemens’ Erlangen factory, agents help prepare new products for production, testing plans in a digital twin before changes reach the factory floor.
And at Dassault Systèmes, engineering agents adapt vehicle design, using simulation to identify a problem and refine the design.
“And [all this] knowledge and tools belong to you,” Huang said after the video rolled. “That’s your expertise, and so all of this is now possible to do.”
Telcos as Distributed AI Infrastructure
Huang said AI is transforming telecommunications, improving spectrum efficiency and turning cell towers into distributed AI infrastructure.
He cited 100,000 sites and about 100 gigawatts of distributed data centers, and said NVIDIA has made its first commercial phone call on T-Mobile’s network with Nokia after nearly eight years of work.
“Now CUDA makes phone calls,” Huang said. “AI will revolutionize the way we do telecommunications. It will enhance our spectrum efficiency tremendously.”
AI Moves Into the Treatment Room
Healthcare and life sciences leaders are building on NVIDIA technologies to advance drug discovery and expand patient care.
For example, NVIDIA and Siemens Healthineers are developing AI-enabled radiation therapy.
Nemotron agents coordinate treatment planning, the Isaac for Healthcare platform and Omniverse libraries create a digital twin of the device and patient anatomy to simulate tumor targeting. Holoscan with IGX Thor connects live imaging and sensor data to enable real-time adaptive delivery as the patient moves.
Huang described adaptive radiotherapy as a physical-AI application: as the patient’s body and tumor change during treatment, the system must track the changes and adjust the radiation targeting.
“The tumor is changing in shape. The physical body is changing while you’re in therapy,” Huang said. “The robot, this radio adaptive radiotherapy system, has to perceive the changing environment, understand where the tumor is, segment it just perfectly and direct the radiotherapy accordingly.”
The Road Ahead: Mobility Leaders Join NVIDIA’s Automotive Ecosystem
Huang said the NVIDIA Hyperion computing platform is being designed into more vehicle fleets, with autonomous-driving software connecting robotaxis to ride-hailing services.
Bolt with Lucid, Mercedes-Benz, Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles and Einride are showcasing selected autonomous-mobility use cases on the NVIDIA Hyperion computing platform, demonstrating potential applications for level 3 and level 4 vehicles as well as future robotaxi fleets.
In addition, Volvo Cars is adopting Hyperion and NVIDIA Alpamayo Stack software for safe automated driving. NVIDIA also introduced new AI and safety technologies to help developers build, validate and deploy autonomous vehicles at scale.
Volkswagen’s van, JLR, Volvo and Mercedes-Benz’s next-generation vehicles will be Hyperion-compatible, Huang announced, saying, “Welcome to Hyperion.”
A Reference Humanoid for Robotics Researchers
Huang then announced Agile ONE SN, a reference humanoid built on Isaac GR00T — a 31-degree-of-freedom body, expected to be available next year, designed to cut researcher setup time from weeks to days.
The platform is modular: researchers can use the full workflow or pull in selected components.
“This is a great starting point,” Huang said.
It builds on NVIDIA’s open physical AI stack — Isaac Capture for data collection, GR00T models for robot intelligence, Isaac Lab for simulation-based training, Isaac OS for runtime — and NVIDIA’s open physical AI dataset. Partners including Agility Robotics, Figure, KUKA and NEURA Robotics are already building on the same platform.
Personal AI Gets a New Machine
Huang closed by discussing RTX Spark laptops, which launched last week, bringing together RTX graphics and NVIDIA’s full-stack AI platform in slim, premium Windows PCs for accelerated creation, immersive gaming and powerful local AI.
He compared its 1 petaflop of performance and 128GB of memory with the DGX-1 he delivered to OpenAI in 2016 — then made the difference in size the punchline:
“In the year 2016, I delivered 1 petaflop and 128GB … to a small company called OpenAI,” Huang said, holding up the compact machine in front of the audience. “This is 1 petaflop and 128GB. The only difference, of course, is that I can hold this like this, and DGX-1 took two people to carry upstairs.”
Huang then showed a video of an agent helping train Hugging Face’s Microduck: it set up a course and simulated the robot in Isaac Sim, sent training jobs to the cloud, then brought the learned policy back to RTX Spark for evaluation before deploying it to the physical robot.
A flock of four Microducks joined Huang onstage, sitting down, standing up and even taking a nap on cue. He explained that they were created on RTX Spark, trained in the cloud and learned their skills in simulation.
“You were created on RTX Spark … [we] trained you in the cloud on a whole bunch of NVIDIA supercomputers, and you learned your skills right here on RTX Spark and the digital twin,” Huang told them.
The Full Lineup
With the Microducks gathered around him, Huang recapped the keynote: Europe is building its AI economy, AI factories are evolving to run agents and physical AI is the next frontier.
“So that’s it,” Huang said. “Everybody can build agents. Every company in Europe will become an AI company … and we’re going to have a thriving AI economy here in Europe.”
To close, Huang had one more surprise: a Eurovision-style musical send-off that turned the keynote’s themes into a comic recap.
The lyrics raced from OpenShell’s guardrails — “No credentials. Access dismissed” and “Sentry on BlueField never clocks off” — to physical AI, where robot training was likened to “college for robots without student loans.”
The punchline: “You can’t spell fungible without fun.” A saxophone solo led into a rousing “We are Europa” chorus.
“Let’s work together to build Europe’s AI economy and put AI to work,” Huang said, closing out his talk. “Have a great GTC.”

articles.title: IDC最新报告：阿里云占中国汽车公共云市场份额超45%
articles.text:
根据国际数据公司（IDC）最新发布的《中国汽车云市场（2026年上半年）跟踪》报告，2026年上半年中国汽车公共云基础设施市场规模约83.4亿元人民币。其中，阿里云市场份额达45.1%，接近半壁江山，在该市场的收入同比增长111%。这也是自2021年起，阿里云已连续11期位居中国汽车公共云基础设施市场第一。
随着大模型在智能座舱、智能辅助驾驶等场景中加速落地，汽车行业对算力资源与AI技术的需求持续增长。阿里云作为提供全栈人工智能服务的全球领导者，凭借以千问大模型、平头哥自研AI芯片，以及高性价比、高稳定性的云计算和AI基础设施，正成为越来越多车企的主流选择。

articles.title: Which Agent's Skill Should Change? Group-Relative Credit Assignment for Evolving Multi-Agent Teams
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.27227v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Cooperative language-model agents can improve without weight updates by revising reusable skills, but only if a shared team reward is traced to the responsible agent and skill. Existing methods credit the skills present in each trajectory, yet presence is not responsibility: a harmful skill active in successful runs still earns positive credit. We present \textbf{GRSE}, \textbf{G}roup-\textbf{R}elative \textbf{S}kill \textbf{E}volution, which assigns behavioral credit by comparison: inspired by GRPO, it executes each question several times under the same skill libraries and contrasts the executions to credit agent--skill pairs, with structured diagnosis of failures. On HotpotQA and LoCoMo with two open-weight actors, GRSE outperforms MASkills, the closest prior method, on HotpotQA and every LoCoMo category except open-domain, with the largest gains on multi-hop questions ($+6.7$ and $+3.2$ F1). Its gains rest on better-grounded retrieval rather than answers given without evidence, and its learned skills transfer between the multi-hop tasks. GRSE is robust to corrupted libraries: starting from planted harmful skills, it credits every planted skill with the correct sign and recovers the score of a clean library ($+6.3$ points), whereas MASkills misattributes two and falls below its starting point.

articles.title: 首都在线：账面扭亏，AI算力持续投入｜看财报
articles.text:
（本文作者为 景行知屿，钛媒体经授权发布）
10月21日，首都在线（300846.SZ）披露2026年三季报，前三季度实现营业收入9.56亿元，同比增长3.14%；归母净利润879.62万元，同比增长108.85%，实现账面扭亏为盈；经营活动产生的现金流量净额2.17亿元，同比大增148.37%。
这是一份"喜忧参半"的成绩单：归母净利润首度转正、经营现金流创近年同期最好水平，但扣非净利润仍亏损5618.03万元；Q3单季毛利率环比跳升近9个百分点的同时，单季营收却同比下滑2.36%；公司资产负债率攀升至68.31%。建设投入仍在消耗资金，未付收购款也带来后续资金需求。盈利尚在修复，公司还要面对新一轮的资本开支，仍在交易所问询环节的15.87亿元定增的重要性不言而喻。
扭亏有“虚火”，经营有改善
单看第三季度，公司营收约2.90亿元，同比下降2.36%；归母净利润却达到4098.12万元，弥补了上半年的亏损。扣非后，当季仍亏638.88万元。
首都在线这次扭亏，主要靠设备处置和政府补助撑起。前三季度，公司处置设备等资产获得收益5542.60万元，列入非经常性损益的政府补助为1719.45万元。计入其他非经常性收支，并扣除所得税及少数股东损益影响后，归母口径非经常性损益净额达到6497.65万元。这笔收益填补了扣非口径下5618.03万元的亏损，才让归母净利润录得879.62万元。
图源：公司第三季报
经营层面，营业成本下降带动了毛利改善。前三季度，公司收入小幅增长，营业成本却由上年同期的8.08亿元降至7.61亿元，毛利同比增加约7637万元。据报表计算，综合毛利率从约12.75%升至20.35%；结合中报测算，第三季度单季毛利率约26.60%，去年同期约为11.91%。
从中报披露的分业务数据看，上半年公司的云业务收入增长较快，IDC业务收入则在下降。上半年，云主机及相关服务收入4.38亿元，同比增长39.67%，占总营收近三分之二；毛利率为15.32%，同比提高10.47个百分点。其中，智算云收入2.39亿元，同比增长107.76%。与提供通用算力的计算云相比，智算云主要依托GPU等高性能算力，服务于模型训练、推理等需求。IDC服务方面，上半年收入2.18亿元，同比下降24.50%，毛利率基本稳定在21.22%，其毛利率仍高于云业务。云业务收入和毛利率同步提升，是公司上半年新增毛利的主要来源。
公司称，正压降同质化、低毛利业务，将资源投向智算基础设施与技术服务。公司在增加自有算力设备的同时，也接入并管理其他企业的算力资源，或通过投资入股等方式与其他企业合作，为客户提供更多算力。
毛利虽然增加了，但仍不足以覆盖期间费用。前三季度，公司实现毛利约1.94亿元，销售、管理、研发和财务四项费用合计约2.26亿元，另有1540.76万元信用减值损失侵蚀利润。不过，同期扣非亏损仍同比收窄51.65%。
现金承压，定增大头仍投AI算力
盈利尚在修复，公司要发展AI算力，还得继续花钱买设备、建机房。前三季度，首都在线经营活动现金流净额为2.17亿元，同比增长148.37%；同期购建固定资产、无形资产和其他长期资产支付的现金达到2.80亿元，超过经营现金净流入约6287万元。9月末，公司现金及现金等价物余额为2.72亿元，较年初减少约1.06亿元。
图源：公司第三季报
与此同时，公司负债水平和利息负担也在上升。按三季报计算，公司期末资产负债率约68.31%，较年初提高近10个百分点，流动负债比流动资产高出约3.73亿元。前三季度利息费用同比增长30.84%，公司解释，主要与2025年下半年新增长期借款、融资租赁直租取得固定资产有关。
公司新增的应付款里，有一大笔是尚未付清的股权收购款。今年6月，公司披露以2.3652亿元收购中嘉和信剩余40%股权，款项分期支付，由实控人曲宁提供担保。到9月末，公司“其他应付款”已从年初的不足5000万元增至2.57亿元。公司称，主要是尚未支付的股权收购款和向实控人借入的资金增加。
中报列明，公司今年2月向实控人曲宁借入合计6000万元，6月末尚未归还，约定于2027年2月到期，公告披露的年利率为4.9%。
在此之外，公司还计划继续扩建算力设施。9月22日披露的募集说明书修订稿显示，15.87亿元拟募资中有2亿元用于偿还银行借款，其余约13.87亿元投向算力建设和研发。其中，约7.87亿元将用于建设怀来算力中心二期，计划建成总功率40兆瓦的机柜，供客户租用、放置服务器，同时提供带宽和专线等配套服务；约5亿元用于智算中心建设，通过租赁第三方机房、购置GPU服务器及配套设备，向客户提供计算资源；约1.01亿元用于天枢智算云研发。
图源：公司公告
从市场层面看，公司向智算倾斜的同时，算力市场的需求也在分化。中信建投研报指出，推理应用正推动持续性算力需求，高端资源供给紧张，部分老旧、中低端资源则面临闲置和价格下行压力。中金公司的推理产业链报告中指出，算力服务的毛利水平受到硬件利用率、采购成本、技术效率和定价能力等因素共同影响。规模扩张有助于摊薄固定成本，但要长期赚钱，还得提高设备使用效率，靠更好的服务增加收入。
就订单而言，公司怀来一期已经找到了客户。中报披露，该项目6月通过竣工验收，7月签下服务协议，将10兆瓦的机柜整体出租给一家大客户。截至9月募集说明书签署日，二期项目已有合计52兆瓦的机柜租用意向，智算中心也有涉及384台高性能服务器的算力服务意向订单。虽然二期租用意向规模已超过规划容量，但两个项目都尚未签订正式协议。
新机房、新设备投入使用后，前期的建设和采购支出也要逐年计入成本。募集说明书测算，募投项目达产后，年新增折旧摊销最高约1.39亿元。设备采购价格也会影响盈利空间：若服务器采购单价上涨10%，其他因素不变，智算中心项目建设运营期预测平均毛利率将下降5.45个百分点。这些新增成本最终能否被项目收入覆盖，仍要看订单落地和设备使用情况。（本文首发于钛媒体APP,文｜景行知屿，作者｜陈析南）

articles.title: OpenAI, Anthropic Should Cap Compute for R&D, Say AI Safety Advocates
articles.text:
Ideas are flowing fast and furious on how AI labs can “pace” AI development so safeguards keep up with the technology’s smarts. Last week, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman laid out three scenarios he said have been considered in the industry, including merging all of the AI labs into a single entity to develop new AI safely or creating a global regulatory body like the International Atomic Energy Agency.
In the background, a loose group of safety advocates and researchers have been pushing for AI companies to cap the amount of compute they put towards research and development, a limitation they argue would be particularly effective in slowing AI development.
The researchers are proposing companies commit to dedicating at least some minimum share of their computational resources to safety or monitoring, and another minimum share to running AI for customers, otherwise known as inference. That would limit the share of compute that could be used to develop stronger AI capabilities through R&D, such as training new models.

articles.title: 五年了还在修！微软承认Win11界面太乱：将动用AI整改缝合UI
articles.text:
快科技10月21日消息，微软产品设计副总裁迭戈・巴卡（Diego Baca）近日在X平台回复博主Chris Pirillo提问时，正面回应了关于Windows 11长期存在界面风格不统一的问题。
他同时透露，微软正在借助AI加快修复这些遗留的视觉设计缺陷。
在回应中，Baca公开承认了Windows用户多年来持续抱怨的设计一致性问题。并表示"Windows跨模块的一致性是大家共同的期望，这目前是一项正在持续推进加速的工作流"。
这一表述间接承认了Windows 11自发布以来在不同功能模块、设置界面与控件样式上长期存在的视觉与交互不统一现象，并明确将其列为团队当前的工作重心之一。
从行业观察视角看，Windows 11自2021年发布至今已历时五年，但系统内部仍存在明显的视觉断层，部分设置面板与对话框仍保留较早时代的UI风格，与新版Fluent Design体系存在明显脱节。
还有部分界面甚至被Windows Latest等媒体指出仍残留Windows 7及更早时代的视觉痕迹。这种新旧UI并存的现象，既是微软长期在系统向后兼容性上的取舍结果，也是设计一致性问题难以根治的根源所在。
目前Baca并未透露AI在Windows 11一致性改造中的具体落地时间表与改造范围，亦未明确"代理舰队"是否会以自动化形式参与系统级UI重构。
但从其表述的整体方向看，AI在微软内部Windows设计流程中的角色正从辅助工具向更深度的参与环节演进，这一趋势的最终效果仍需观察后续Windows 11功能更新中所呈现的实际改造幅度。

articles.title: Beyond Model Weights: Sampling-Dependent Fairness in Diffusion Language Models
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.27584v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Diffusion language models (DLMs) are emerging as a practical alternative to autoregressive language models (ARLMs), yet their fairness remains largely uncharacterized. DLMs introduce sampling controls with no direct autoregressive counterpart, such as block length and remasking strategy, that directly set their speed--quality operating point. This raises a basic question: does a DLM's measured social bias remain stable across these settings? Across LLaDA, LLaDA-1.5, and Dream on Open-BBQ, we find that all three models exhibit social bias, but both the magnitude of measured bias and the relative ordering of models by bias are highly sensitive to the sampling configuration. This sampling dependence also changes what successful debiasing means. While mitigation strategies established for ARLMs transfer effectively to DLMs and reduce bias without degrading downstream performance, sampling dependence persists even after mitigation. Our results show that fairness in DLMs cannot be characterized independently of the sampling configuration, even after debiasing. Project page is available at https://pakapaka333.github.io/Beyond-Model-Weights/.

articles.title: AutoTerm-SST: Adaptive Terminology Memory with Zero Session-Time Setup for Streaming Speech Translation
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.26865v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Retrieval-augmented speech translation improves rare terminology, but systems such as RASST still assume that users provide a glossary before each session. That assumption is inconvenient for live talks, while merging every domain into one growing glossary eventually places too many irrelevant terms in the same retrieval and prompt competition. We present AutoTerm-SST, an interactive system that removes session-time glossary upload and domain selection. It organizes a large offline terminology catalog into topic slices, matches recent streaming translation context to bilingual slice prototypes, and activates a compact multi-slice working set under fixed retrieval and prompt budgets. On five ACL and five ESO oncology talks, AutoTerm matches a known-domain reference in terminology accuracy (88.3% vs. 88.1%) and mWER-resegmented BLEU (45.09 vs. 45.19), while requiring no domain input. Compared with a one-million-entry merged glossary, it improves terminology accuracy by 3.9 points and BLEU by 2.30. Routing plus four-slice retrieval remains lightweight: the complete system runs at 0.406 RTF, and the vLLM host sustains 32 real-time sessions. The live demo exposes active slices and retrieved terminology as the topic changes, providing zero-setup terminology-aware streaming translation.

articles.title: 蔚来李斌：用户不愿意付钱 自动驾驶讲得再好也没用
articles.text:
快科技10月21日消息，今日，在2026世界智能网联汽车大会的对话环节上，蔚来创始人李斌针对自动驾驶行业当下的发展阶段发表了自己的看法。
在他看来，自动驾驶已经步入发展的下半场，行业评价技术好坏，不能只看炫酷的功能演示，应当回归两项可以实际验证的核心标尺，以此判断技术是否真正为用户创造价值。
其中第一个关键衡量维度，就是用户的付费意愿。李斌提出，即便一套自动驾驶技术对外宣传的性能再出众，如果用户不愿意为之买单，就谈不上实现真实的用户价值。
第二项重要评判标准，则是安全性能要做到可量化、可被用户切身感知，让用户实实在在体会到智驾比人工驾驶更加安全。
会上李斌公布了蔚来辅助驾驶的最新运行统计成果，这套系统累计行驶里程突破91.4亿公里，总使用时长超1.12亿小时，已经完成超过907万次事故规避或是风险减轻。
同时结合四家保险机构的联合评估数据，2026年上半年，蔚来车辆依靠主动安全功能，整体事故损失下降38.4%，人车协同驾驶模式下的安全里程，达到纯人工驾驶的八倍。
对于未来技术演进方向，李斌判断，行业技术路线会逐步向世界模型搭配闭环强化学习靠拢。
从L2到L5等级，底层技术架构具备同源属性，真正能够拉开各家产品安全上限差距的，是整车冗余设计、算力配置规模以及传感器硬件的综合实力。

articles.title: Benefit and Cost of Random-Token Replacement under Repeated Data: A Known-Entropy Decomposition and Evidence from Ten Real Corpora
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.27590v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: When unique pretraining data is scarce, models see the same tokens many times and are thought to memorize. Random-token replacement, an input-corruption augmentation, is one remedy reported to lower validation loss, but a lower loss alone does not reveal which source of error it reduces. On a controlled source whose entropy rate is known in closed form, we show that replacement shrinks predictions toward the corpus average. We also introduce a decomposition that separates validation loss into approximation, estimation, and memorization terms. This shrinkage view predicts that replacement's bias cost needs no memorization but its benefit does. Memorization raises validation loss after its minimum, so we report the effect at two points, the minimum validation loss and the end of a fixed budget. Where replacement helps, it reduces this rise by about 60%. At the end of the budget, it turns from harmful to helpful as the controlled source becomes less predictable; at the minimum, it helps at no predictability level under the fixed recipe. On Korean and Japanese web text, replacement removes about a third of the loss rise after the minimum by the end of the budget, but its effect at the minimum is much smaller. Across ten real corpora, replacement lowers the final loss on nine. It harms only the census corpus, program-generated JSON that is the most redundant of the ten and much more redundant than any of 64 further prose and code corpora we measure.

articles.title: Explore More, Validate Less: Efficient Reflective Prompt Optimization
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.27367v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Reflective prompt optimization improves instructions using task feedback, but coupling candidate generation with full-validation-based selection can make search costly and sequential. We propose a two-stage framework that decouples reflective candidate-pool construction from validation allocation. During construction, we sample multiple parents and reuse each parent's training responses across parallel reflection branches. Each revision is screened against its parent on a small training minibatch, allowing locally improved candidates to support further revisions without full validation. After construction, an exploration policy selects candidates from the frozen pool under a fixed full-validation budget, and the prompt with the highest measured validation score is returned. This separation allows candidate-pool size and validation budget to be set independently. We evaluate random selection and learned score prediction with similarity-based exploration on five benchmarks using Qwen3.5-9B and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. With 100 retained candidates and 20 full validations, our framework improves over the initial solver by up to 11.22 percentage points. Learned selection improves over the initial solver in all ten comparisons, although neither selection policy consistently outperforms the other. These results support separating reflective search from budgeted validation while leaving room for stronger candidate-selection policies.

不止颜值出众，荣耀WIN2还配备精研雾面金属中框，整机支持IP68+IP69+IP69K超可靠防尘防水，颜值、手感、耐用性全面兼顾。

articles.title: The Huawei-DeepSeek Symbiosis
articles.text:
Right before China’s national day holidays, DeepSeek released Ascend support for TileLang, DeepGEMM, DeepEP, TileKernels, FlashMLA, and DeepSelect.
Neither can do this alone. Although they have Pangu, Huawei has no frontier lab to prove their chip can train or infer models, DeepSeek has models but cannot buy the compute it needs. Each supplies exactly what the other lacks: Huawei provides the hardware and native software stack; DeepSeek brings the workloads and engineering needed to make that hardware useful for its models. September 30’s release of Ascend support in DeepSeek repositories is an artifact of this trade, where the exchange runs through the kernel-authoring language.
Source: SemiAnalysis - Note that the diagram is a simulation.
In 2028 or even 2027, DeepSeek will likely be primarily using Huawei’s stack, especially with the external and internal pressure to build a fully domestic chinese ecosystem. As we show here and in future articles, the Huawei ecosystem is already mature and well developed, with strong foundations from the Ascend time and DeepSeek engineers building further ontop.
In this article, we’ll first examine Ascend 950PR’s architecture and benchmark its compute and memory performance. We then explore DeepSeek’s software releases, from TileLang’s compiler capabilities to hardware-specific kernel optimizations and rack-scale communication. Finally, we analyze DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash’s execution profile.
Ascend 950
We deep-dived into CANN and the Ascend 950 architecture in our DeepSeek V4 Pro article. Since then, more interesting details have been revealed.
Source: SemiAnalysis
Starting from the chip, many variants of 950PR/DT have appeared with varying core counts, HBM stack height, and cache sizes. Some are likely either virtualised/simulated, or for testing only. This is because only a fraction of dies and HBM stacks meet the target spec, due to both outright defects and parametric shortfalls in power and performance, so Huawei bins both compute and memory into multiple SKUs and pairs weaker memory with weaker compute, rather than binning only compute as Nvidia does.
Source: SemiAnalysis
This isn’t new, 910B also has variants such as 910B1, 910B2, 910B3, 910B4. For the following microbenchmarks, we use an Ascend 950PR_9579, with 28 cube cores and 128 GiB HBM.
root@cb3bb851f93f:/workspace# npu-smi info
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| npu-smi 25.7.rc1.6                               Version: 25.7.rc1.6                            |
+--------+------------------+---------------+-----------------------------------------------------+
| NPU ID | Name             | Health        | Power(W)    Temp(C)           Hugepages-Usage(page) |
|        |                  | Bus-Id        | NPU Util(%) Memory-Usage(MB)  HBM-Usage(MB)         |
+========+==================+===============+=====================================================+
| 0      | Ascend950PR      | OK            | 203.3       56                0     / 0             |
|        |                  | 0000:12:00.0  | 0           0    / 0          5242  / 131072        |
+========+==================+===============+=====================================================+
+---------------------------+---------------+-----------------------------------------------------+
| NPU ID                    | Process id    | Process name             | Process memory(MB)       |
+===========================+===============+=====================================================+
| No running processes found in NPU 0                                                             |
+===========================+===============+=====================================================+
Running point chases reading 16 KiB of integer payload per launch, it stays near 134ns through 18 blocks, rises to 182ns at 56, then jumps to 391ns at 64. This is consistent with a second wave beyond 56 Vector cores.
Source: SemiAnalysis
Then by running a scalar pointer-chase probe separately on every Cube and Vector core, recording load timings at matching addresses throughout a 128 MiB chain, we get the following graph. Each cell’s color represents the mean absolute difference between two cores' address profiles, producing two groups that match the decoded dies.
Source: SemiAnalysis
Going further, by timing a Vector core’s pointer chase while another core runs either memory traffic or register-only work; the extra slowdown reveals which subsystems share resources, supporting groups such as {0,2,4} and {1,3,5}. Mixed Cube/Vector launches identify each subsystem’s one Cube and two Vectors, which we draw together within those groups, with physical positions remaining schematic.
Source: SemiAnalysis
CPU within the NPU
Each 950PR comes with a variable number of Linx816 AArch64 ELF AICPUs. The MIDR numbers imply these cores are likely the same as the middle cores in the Kirin 9000S/9010. These AICPU cores have instruction set:
fp asimd evtstrm aes pmull sha1 sha2 crc32 atomics fphp asimdhp cpuid
asimdrdm jscvt fcma lrcpc dcpop sha3 sm3 sm4 asimddp sha512 sve
asimdfhm dit uscat ilrcpc flagm ssbs sb paca pacg dcpodp flagm2
frint svei8mm svebf16 i8mm bf16 dgh rng ecv
For this SKU, there are 7 configured, 6 visible, and 5 executing AICPU cores. Other than device control it can provide CPU-operator support, such as KV metadata. The AICPU helps out for short work where D2H overhead take up most of the time.
For DSA, a small scheduling step reads the current sequence lengths and assigns indexer work to accelerator cores. Cube/Vector cores then compute INT8 indexer scores and select the top 2,048 indices. These planning, index selection, and gather steps are ran on AICPUs in vLLM-ascend implementation, and we compare their performance to running on the host CPU.
Source: SemiAnalysis
Due to their limited compute performance, AICPU is only good for short work where overhead dominates, and work where data starts and is consumed at the NPU.
Microbenchmarks
Ascend 950PR is designed for prefill and recommendation. It gets lower memory bandwidth and core than its bigger brother the 950DT.
The results below are not from DeepSeek’s contributions but from stock torch.matmul on ascend resolving to aclnnMatmul_MatMulV3Common_MatMulV3. We compared 1,055 BF16 GEMM shapes from several open-sourced models. Huawei’s best kernels hits 99.7% of the ceiling, showing DeepSeek’s 99+% from DeepGEMM isn’t the only way to maximize utilization. Huawei engineers did good work too.
Source: SemiAnalysis
The advantage is concentrated in compute-bound work. On the shapes below Ascend’s ridge, its median achieved/attainable fraction is 41.5% versus H100’s 46.8%. Some of Nvidia’s results were power-limited and did not hit maximum SM clock: median power around 690-698 W out of a 700 W limit, and median sampled SM clocks at 1335-1470 MHz, below the max of 1830 MHz. Huawei approximated 599-600 W, at 1500-1550 MHz against its 1650 MHz reference.
Ascend’s MXU design may contribute to some of this high utilization, Ascend stages matrix operands in dedicated L0A/L0B buffers and accumulators in L0C, with overlapping movement, computation and result handling. Huawei associates the enlarged L0C with more flexible tiling and reuse.
But of course, 950PR’s falls behind on absolute values, sitting somewhere between A100 and MI300X.
Source: SemiAnalysis
MemBW
Measuring HBM memory bandwidth, we see 950PR’s effective bandwidth and bandwidth utilization surpassing H100 at small message size per buffers, and nearly matching H100 in bandwidth utilization at large message sizes.
Source: SemiAnalysis
A dip appears in the curve as Ascend switches copy methods to a Vector-core TensorMove kernel that has more startup cost, so a slightly larger copy suddenly takes longer. For very large copies, that extra cost becomes relatively small, so bandwidth rises again.
Note that high FLOPs utilization and bandwidth utilization does not necessarily translate to high MFU/MBU. Training, especially with FSDP, requires collectives, checkpointing, and data moving that can be hard to overlap.
As we mentioned in our Jalepeno article, a “chip” in benchmarks is just a social construct. Multiple dies can be glue to form a bigger “chip”.  Thus performance per watt or TCO is the best comparison. But for China, watts are far cheaper. We’ll analyze Ascend’s perf per TCO in a future article.
Hardware raises the ceiling, but software lets you reach that ceiling. Although Huawei’s hardware may be beyond ~5 years behind(compared to A100), the software is right at the frontier.
DeepSeek Open Source
For the 6 repos that received ascend support(TileLang, DeepGEMM, DeepEP, TileKernels, FlashMLA, DeepSelect), only TileLang is usable as of writing, and CANN 9.2.0 has not been released. Deepseek requires CANN 9.2.0 which was released after time of writing, and a C++20 compiler is required which CANN 9.2.0-beta.2 does not provide. The HDK will be released on Oct 15. This comes after DeepSeek’s open source week in 2025, where some of these repositories were released with Nvidia support only.
From the results above, we can see Huawei can already execute operations well; the symbiosis is about making the rest of the application & the work required to support it more efficient and reusable.
Engineering runs both ways
Huawei’s architecture is already influencing how DeepSeek’s software organizes data. Earlier FlashMLA KV-cache layouts stored quantized values and their scaling factors in separate regions. On Ascend, fetching a token then required separate transfers for its values and scales. The new implementation places them together, reducing the number of transfer requests by the memory transfer engine(MTE).
Source: SemiAnalysis
From fast kernels to reusable kernel engineering
Ascend 950 backend is merged into the main TileLang repository, rather than existing only in a separate Huawei adapter. It adds native compilation, scheduling, synchronization and runtime integration for Ascend’s execution model.
TileLang makes Ascend kernels easier to write, but developers still need to account for the hardware. They choose the calculations, tile sizes and where data is stored. The compiler handles much of the coordination between Cube cores, Vector cores and data transfers.
Digging below the implementation and looking at its performance against CANN and Triton-ascend, it can match and beat CANN at certain cases; the preferred implementation changes with size.  This is a warm-cache simple and naive benchmark.
Source: SemiAnalysis
AutoSchedule uses data dependencies and estimated execution times to plan which operations can overlap. It also chooses how many buffer slots to use within the available on-chip memory, allowing upcoming data to load while the current tile is being processed. Developers can guide these decisions when the default schedule is not suitable.
Source: SemiAnalysis
On 950PR, AutoSchedule helps especially for smaller sizes, reducing execution time by up to 40% for a single operation.
Source: SemiAnalysis
The compiler also inserts synchronization so operations wait for the data they need, while removing waits that other dependencies make unnecessary. It checks conditional branches too, so it does not assume an operation has completed when that branch might never execute. This reduces the synchronization work programmers must manage themselves.
DeepEP
Huawei has joined NVIDIA in commercializing large scale-up AI systems, with its Ascend supernodes extending tightly coupled accelerator interconnects across multiple racks from the 910 CloudMatrix384 to the 950 SuperPod,enabling wideEP scale-out. In the 30th September release, Huawei also released EP16 dispatch/combine benchmarks over URMA in the 950DT superpod.
Source: Huawei, DeepSeek, SemiAnalysis
Huawei’s dispatch is three sequential operators (pre/URMA/post) whereas GB300 is one fused call, and their post work includes receive completion, which our measurement includes, but also includes expansion by expert which GB300’s results don’t.
DeepEP-Ascend is a port of DeepEP V2.5, with the same python API but calls URMA and HCCL underneath. In July 2025, Huawei’s Ascend team proposed DeepEP-Ascend under deepseek-ai, but a DeepEP maintainer declined. Today, DeepEP-Ascend is distributed under DeepSeek’s own organization.
Ascend’s separate Cube and Vector execution paths create opportunities to overlap communication and computation, but do not make that overlap free. Expert computation can also require vector processing and data movement, while communication competes for shared memory bandwidth. Therefore there’s a tradeoff on how much communication can be hidden without slowing the computation that runs alongside.
Source: Huawei
This resource-balancing problem is not unique to DeepSeek. Huawei’s Kimi K3 recipe explicitly restricts vector use to leave capacity for concurrent work, and chooses between dedicated CCU and Vector-based communication according to what must overlap. Faster individual operations are not enough: their resource demands must also fit together.
DeepEP-Ascend’s documentation identifies contention between combine processing and URMA communication for HBM resources, and says Huawei firmware improvements are planned to reduce it. This is the practical form of co-design: the model exposes a bottleneck, the implementation adapts, and the platform’s development priorities respond to what remains.
All planned
In May’s unverified DeepSeek investor meeting transcript, Liang Wenfeng said:
“So, when it comes to the chip gap between China and the US, I think the software ecosystem gap will eventually disappear. But on the hardware side, we face two separate disadvantages: it takes four Huawei accelerator cards to match one NVIDIA card, and Huawei is also roughly two years behind in bringing its hardware to market.”
4 months later, the ecosystem gap did indeed narrow. The same transcript mentioned TileLang and helping Huawei get the ecosystem right.
DSv4.1 Flash Optimizations
Another part of the DeepSeek-Huawei symbiosis is that DeepSeek provides Huawei with weights, supporting Day-0 optimized releases, such as DeepSeek V4 and V4.1.
Ascend’s accumulator design forces a different approach to attention. The Cube’s L0C buffer cannot rescale accumulated outputs in place, while returning a rescaled output to L0C would require an expensive identity-matrix multiplication. DeepSeek instead keeps the running output accumulator in Vector UB, transferring partial sums from L0C when needed for rescaling and accumulation. Hopper holds its accumulator in registers, while Blackwell provides loads and stores between tensor memory and registers, avoiding this particular restriction
Source: SemiAnalysis
Profile
Huawei also released a profile of one rank of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on a Huawei Ascend 950DT deployment of 32 chips, together with its host threads. In June, we covered a similar profile, that of DeepSeek V4 Pro’s.
Many components are similar, like the use of AICPU and separation of some layers to different streams.
Source: SemiAnalysis
The execution order is 40 target-model layers, the target LM head, 3 DSpark drafter blocks, the draft LM head, and 5 sampling rounds. The main compute runs on Stream 19; the drafter’s run on Stream 173. The V2 MC² kernels that fused computation and communication from the DSv4 Pro trace shows up again, as V3 this time. This is why only 4 AI CPU-launched HCCL operations appear per step, against 43 expert dispatches. These are the target and draft vocabulary heads’ hcom_allGather and hcom_alltoallv: gather hidden states, run the LM-head GEMM, then exchange logits.
The drafter blocks run once to produce base logits for the draft positions. The subsequent Markov head models token dependencies through sampling and embedding feedback. It does not rerun the transformer blocks for each proposal. The end of each step changes from MoE and a

articles.title: 现在复活一款老游戏 只需要8小时了
articles.text:
如果你最近常刷视频，不难发现一个现象，那就是很多陪你度过童年与青春无数个夜晚，最后却惨遭关服的网游手游们，像是 QQ 堂、使命召唤 OL、妖怪正传、少女咖啡枪、乖离性百万亚瑟王等，成功打赢了复活赛。
复活它们的不是游戏官方，而是一些没啥名气，甚至粉丝只有几百几千的小博主们。
复活老游戏不是什么新鲜话题，但批量复活，复活的还是网游，复活后还能联机对战，那就很夸张了。
可以允许高手在民间，但民间高手。。。是不是有点太多了？
小发之所以质疑，是因为复活老游戏这活，听着就是新瓶装老酒，简单搞搞就完事了，实际上，这份工作相当牛马，纯粹是用爱发电的苦力活。
一些自己搞过复活老游戏的老哥应该知道，干不好白费功夫，浪费的时间以年为单位；干好了也赚不到钱，还很容易收律师函，可能自己都不知道图啥。
人工复活老游戏工程量有多大呢？
最近正好有个例子，2020 年的时候有一堆人拉了个群，想要把一代人的回忆，Gameloft《狂野飙车 8：极速凌云》的老版本做成单机。
这一折腾，就是 6 年多。6 年多啊朋友，六年级小学生都上大一了。
直到前阵子的 10 月 3 日，一个相对完善的版本才做完并对外发布。
为啥这么费劲呢？
因为他们做的不是破解版，而是一个基于单机模式，优化所有系统的版本。
比如游戏里和氪金相关的代币系统，变成了无关氪金的积分系统；赛制方面，加入了新的单车经典模式；游戏新增了自定义匹配功能，玩家输入 Rank 分，系统就会自动生成接近相关分段的 AI 选手，用来模拟原本的 PVP。。。
要是说这个团队一半精力在折腾游戏本身系统上的优化，那另一半的精力，就是在想办法让它适应当下的设备和系统。
现在我们的软件硬件比过去强了无数倍，但很多老游戏是没法运行的。
像是十年前的《地下城与勇士》的女枪版和男鬼剑版，你千辛万苦下载好安装包，打开就直接闪退了，很多普通玩家想重温，只能去二手市场淘旧机。
游戏仙人们利用游戏资源，手搓单机版，要花6年时间。有了对比，你才能感觉这个游戏大复活时代的反常。
提问：你猜猜现在那些批量复活的网游手游们，花了多长时间？
直接公布答案——快的话，不到半天，只需要几个小时。这几个小时里，你甚至不用敲一行代码，只需要发出命令，当个键盘指挥官就行。
可能有人已经猜到了，游戏大复活时代的根本，就是AI的神力。
B 站 UP “ 今天风甚是喧嚣 ”，粉丝只有 103 个，他只投稿了一个视频，那就是用 AI 把 Com2us 的《妙战天下》给复活了。
复活的过程和复杂不沾边，甚至给人一种我上我也行的感觉，戏谑到有点难绷。
省流一下：全程 7 小时 53 分，用掉了约 10.8 亿token，只给 AI 发了 52 条消息。
别说你了，我都有点怀疑这家伙是不是虚报数字了——52 条消息，不是哥们，我有时候写稿查资料，给 AI 发的消息随随便便就超过 52 条了。
10.8 亿token，对外行来说看着是挺唬人，但对开发者而言，真没多少。
换成钞票，10 亿 token 贵的能有几千几万甚至更贵，便宜的也是真便宜，前阵子有个副局长 10 亿 token 手搓小程序的新闻，他也就花了 20 块人民币，比我的话费都便宜。
《妙战天下》复活的流程，解释起来也不复杂。
UP 先是用 AI 找到了游戏的安装包，不过因为服务器早已关停，所以安装包基本等同于一个空壳，支撑游戏运行的资产，比如角色、关卡、数值，这些都没有。
一般情况下，到这一步已经完犊子了，AI 也巧妇难为无米之炊，没招了。
但现实已经无数次证明世界就是个草台班子，UP 拍拍脑袋，对 AI 说资源可能就在 CDN 上，AI 就这么水灵灵的把资源给找到了。。。
简单来讲，游戏之前通过 CDN，也就是距离玩家最近的服务器传输信息，但停服后，这些服务器上的资源没删，还任君随意零元购，这就是互联网共享精神吗，泪目了。
接着就是让 AI 把资源对号入座，一些缺的数值，AI 还自己扒了当年玩家的攻略给补上了。最后它还测试了一波发现能跑通，才输出了最终版本。
而 UP 主本人，打了几行字，睡了个觉，天亮了就可以玩了。
是的朋友们，这事就这么简单，你上你真行。
我们已经无从找起谁拉开了大复活时代的大幕，但网上，人们似乎不约而同的，开始找起了那些承载自己青春回忆的游戏安装包，对着电脑大喊 “ 复活吧我的爱人 ”。
于是，我们能玩到当代所有二游的爷，2012 年发布 2018 年国服停运的乖离性百万亚瑟王，甚至还有 PC 端，享受到了老一辈都没经历过的体验。
我们还能玩到曾经无数人的遗憾，运营八年却于 2024 年一度被迫停服的《少女前线》。
此外，还有天命之子、梅露可物语、魔塔大陆2、苍之纪元、永远的七日之都等一大堆游戏，都被人们从某个犄角旮旯挖出来，堂堂复活。
每当人们发现自己一度痴迷的游戏秽土转生，前一秒还在家祭无忘告乃翁，下一秒就垂死病中惊坐起，快乐溢出了屏幕。
动手能力强点的，可以配合 AI 搓个自己喜欢的版本。
动手能力弱点的，直接在评论区许愿。
随着大复活时代声势越发浩大，人们对于 “ 复活 ” 的标准也越来越高。
最开始，人们觉得只要游戏能跑起来，自己能正常玩就行。
发展到后边，很多人已经开始给一些原先具备联网功能的游戏，搭起了各种联机系统。
比如一个千人粉丝小 UP 复活的 QQ 堂，用了 50 亿 token，恢复了绝大部分功能，还做出了本地、局域网以及网络联机等功能的适配，兼容 Windows 10、11。
这种勃勃生机、万物竞发的景象，是不是让你不由感叹技术塑造美好生活了呢？
诶，先别偷着乐，大复活时代很行，也很刑。
伴随着无数游戏的复活，有人想过，既然可以复活过去的游戏，那是不是也意味着可以把现在还运营的游戏也做成本地版。
这个大胆的想法，很快就被创作者圈子踩住了刹车，毕竟喜提银手镯这件事，谁都不想沾上。
可玩家们讲究个圈地自萌，只想享受简单的快乐，倒狗哪管你这的那的。
各种平台上，倒卖复活版游戏赚钱的人早就泛滥了。
你烧了几十亿 token，熬了几个夜，做出来和同好一起玩的游戏，转头就被拿走，然后挂个两块八毛八，在其他地方售卖。
销量有多少不好说，主要是恶心人，恶心你，也恶心游戏厂商。
所谓的大复活时代，说难听点就是大私服时代、大盗版时代，本质还是利用游戏厂商的已有资源还原游戏内容。
如果只是小圈子里自娱自乐，可能厂商也就睁一只眼闭一只眼，当做无事发生。
毕竟这两年，停止杀死游戏的玩家运动如火如荼，想要游戏 “ 永生 ” 是所有玩家的一致诉求。
国内可能相对来说氛围比较和谐，没有太多玩家和厂商因为这件事硬刚。
厂商们做单机陪伴服的也少，心虚之下，自然也对这种擦边球的大复活运动高抬贵手，当然，也是觉得无所吊谓，让全民制作人自己手搓又何妨。
这种思路很正常，因为那些被复活的游戏，本身就是不适应市场潮流才被关闭。
平时可能还有点讨论度，但真做出来，只会是小圈子里的三分钟热度。
就像英雄联盟经典模式一样，之前一堆人讨论老卡萨丁多变态、AP 剑圣多牛逼、利刃华尔兹多超模，真做出来狗都不玩，上线三个月，就官宣不再常驻，要在 2027 年 1 月关闭。
去年 17173 也搞了个投票，让玩家给停运的老游戏投票，达到一定票数后，他们就代表玩家去和运营方沟通，推动游戏复活。
目前票数最多的游戏叫《机甲旋风》，只有 13804 票，进度卡在了寻找版权方，复活遥遥无期。
游戏厂商其实也很无奈，因为复活老游戏不是拍拍脑袋就能决定的事，即便不考虑能不能收回成本的问题，也要受到很多因素影响。
可还是那句话，我可以不玩，你不能没有。
最好的情况是官方自己搞个单机陪伴版，既然没有，那把权利下放给玩家群体，还算说的过去。
但是兄弟，光明正大售卖 “ 复活版 ”，这已经不是很跳了，这是对厂商的挑衅。
二手贩子啥时候收到律师函不好说，有些想要复活游戏的创作者，可能会因此放弃；游戏厂商，也会逐渐收紧那些原本被遗忘在互联网角落里的开放资源；AI 被套上枷锁，几乎成了板上钉钉的事。
三月份的时候，我们采访过一位纯靠 AI，一行代码不写，在网页和移动端复刻了《新剑侠情缘》、《月影传说》、《剑侠情缘 2》的大佬，当时还在感慨，开发独立游戏时，AI 早晚会包揽代码工作。
谁也没想到，这个感慨，实现的如此之快，以至于人们还没反应过来。
10 月 16 日，运营了两年的逆向工程反编译社区 decomp.dev 宣布关停，公告中很明确的提到人工+AI 能显著加快反编译过程。
但压垮社区的原因，还是因为氛围烂了，有人滥用 AI，疯狂搞“移植版”游戏，把反编译从热爱与研究变成机械化流水线式的 AI 破解。
这就是现实的悲哀，当我们意识到自己处在大复活时代的黄金时期，却已经可以预判到这个所谓的时代，终究会昙花一现般草草收场。
话题又回到了 AI 上，难道对着现有的游戏用 AI 二创，就绝对没有未来吗？也不尽然。
把 B 社口碑砸了的星空，用了八年时间还没做出来无缝着陆，而 MOD 开发者，借助 AI 工具，一个人用了半年时间就解决了这个问题。
技术在发展，掌握着 AI 这个大杀器的人们，有着各种各样的想法，他们也会踏上不同的道路。
有人向左，有人向右，有人一往直前，但没有人会逆着时代，一路转身向后。

articles.title: 电竞手机比拼逻辑变了，荣耀WIN2选择“用价换量”
articles.text:
（本文作者为 志读科技，钛媒体经授权发布）
今年的手机市场，只能用一个“难”字形容。伴随着存储、芯片等供应链成本高企，终端手机市场也进行了多轮的涨价，整个行业进入到存量竞争深化阶段，品牌面临着市场策略调整以及行业争议的双重考验。
但这并没有影响到手机厂商的出牌节奏。从9月底到现在，基本上所有的主流品牌都发布了新款旗舰机。只是，高涨的价格，让销量相比较去年同期大打折扣。
其中，电竞手机作为一个相对的小众品类，凭借精准的玩家定位和差异化的性能体验，在大盘下行的环境中始终保持着话题热度。只不过，全新的竞争环境下，电竞手机不单单是比拼性能，更是生态与价格的多重考验。
近段时间，多家厂商相继更新了旗下的电竞系列。今天下午，荣耀就对外发布了荣耀WIN2、荣耀WIN RT2两款电竞旗舰，性能之外，还采用了全新的定价策略，希望通过价格上的优势在这波震荡周期中寻求更多的销量。
值得一提的是，在发布会的一开始，荣耀中国区副总裁林林就“冒犯”了一下友商，吐槽现在的手机发布会早已不属于数码领域，而是文化领域，击穿边界、底层创新等等各种词，让消费者觉得自己配不上发布的新机。不仅如此，林林连自家产品也没放过，称现在的手机名字也是越来越长。
经过数年发展，电竞手机赛道内卷早已脱离了单纯的“堆芯片、拼参数”阶段，正向全维度体验和生态协同延伸。从配置上来看，荣耀WIN2在性能上堆料很足，搭载第六代骁龙8超级至尊版，根据荣耀实验室数据，其安兔兔综合性能跑分高达5702964分。并支持AI渲显分离，1%Low帧提升20FPS。
在主动风扇散热成为性能旗舰主流标配的今天，荣耀WIN2采用双风扇设计，官方宣称散热性能提升150%，同风量风噪降低9dB，总风量提升284%，可实现50秒直降10℃。还标配2K 185Hz双芯绿洲屏，支持40+款原生高刷游戏。
除了手机之外，荣耀开始将电竞从单一终端延伸至产品矩阵，推出了荣耀WIN平板和荣耀WIN耳机等新品，组成了荣耀WIN电竞生态。这意味着，厂商争夺的不再只是一部游戏手机的销量，也包括玩家在不同设备和场景中的体验入口。不过，生态能否真正形成竞争壁垒，最终仍取决于设备之间能否产生实际的协同价值，而不只是产品数量的增加。
另外，当核心配置不断趋同，价格便成为影响消费者选择的重要变量，尤其是今年。对于电竞手机而言，这道题更难：芯片、散热系统、超高刷屏幕和大容量电池都需要额外投入，硬件越堆越高，成本也随之增加。荣耀WIN2延续了此前Magic9系列的定价策略，首销国补到手价分别为4999元起，WIN RT2国补价3149元起。
之所以如此定价，原因很简单，在行业下行、消费趋于理性的周期里，荣耀选择主动舍弃单品利润，用性价比换取市场规模和用户份额。荣耀CEO李健曾表示，行业所有厂家都在承受内存暴涨带来的成本压力，但荣耀会尽量在内部消化，不能把压力全部转嫁给用户。
从市场反馈来看，这套 “以价换量” 的策略确实已经显现效果。根据IDC数据显示，二季度中国手机市场前六品牌中，只有荣耀实现了增长。在新一轮的旗舰机比拼中，荣耀也是增长较快的那一个。
只不过，一个无法回避的问题是：这种牺牲利润换规模的模式，到底能坚持多久？就连荣耀自身在发布会上也坦言，存储的价格每天都在变化，并不确定这种低价策略能够持续多长时间。
而这，不只是荣耀需要回答的问题，更是表面热闹的手机产业面临的新考题：当性能越来越强、成本越来越高，如何能在用户体验与商业回报之间，找到一条可持续的路？

articles.title: H2DF: Calibrated Target Bands for Controllable Language-Model Unlearning
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.26864v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Gradient ascent (GA) is a simple language-model unlearning baseline, but it continues increasing forget loss after useful forgetting has occurred. This unbounded pressure can damage retained utility and make forgotten examples abnormally high-loss. We introduce H2DF, a calibrated target-band objective that applies GA-like pressure below a data-dependent lower target and suppresses, or reverses, that pressure after the target region is reached. The targets are estimated from matched non-member examples before training, so the base objective requires one forget-batch forward/backward pass per optimization step; our reported TOFU variant adds sparse retain replay every tenth step. We instantiate a one-sided objective for TOFU question answering and a two-sided objective for MUSE-News language modeling. Across three TOFU seeds, H2DF obtains a forget NLL of 1.528 with margin 0.049 and retain NLL of 1.165 with margin 0.047, matching GradDiff while using retain replay only every tenth step and showing substantially lower variability than GA. On MUSE-News, H2DF improves retention over GA and NPO and is competitive with SimNPO, but does not dominate it. Ablations show that the upper target reduces overshoot and that validation-based checkpoint selection is important. These results support calibrated target bands as a practical mechanism for controlling forgetting strength, while also exposing sensitivity to random seed and calibration quality.

articles.title: AMD炮轰TOPS指标过时！物理AI要的是毫秒级保命 不是跑分
articles.text:
快科技10月21日消息，据报道，AMD自适应与嵌入式计算集团高级副总裁兼总经理Salil Raje近日在官方博客中公开批评，传统的AI芯片跑分指标（如TOPS）已无法充分衡量物理AI系统的真实性能。
因为物理AI面临的是真实物理世界的严苛约束，纸面上的峰值算力并不等同于实际执行能力。对于机器人制造商而言，最需要是将先进模型与在规定时限内精确执行计算结果的实时控制能力相结合。
在传统AI领域，业界习惯用TOPS等跑分数据来衡量芯片性能，但Raje指出，这套评价体系在物理AI时代已经失效。物理AI要求机器人在真实环境中感知、推理并执行物理动作。
如果AI模型算得再快，却因数据搬运或调度延迟错过了毫秒级的控制窗口，结果不是卡顿，而是碰撞和翻车。因此，平均延迟远远不够，跑分高不代表不会出事，系统必须抑制延迟抖动和最大延迟。
为应对这一挑战，AMD提出了仿生异构架构，将机器人比作人体。
大脑负责感知与推理，由锐龙AI嵌入式X100系列处理器的Kria AI模块承担；脊椎负责确定性通信与整合，由Versal自适应SoC充当；关节的精密运动控制交给Zynq SoC；传感器的一级处理则由Spartan FPGA完成。
不同任务交给最适合的计算引擎，从而突破带宽、功耗和延迟的瓶颈。
据AMD引用的第三方测试，Kria AI SOM实现了低于0.1秒的AI推理时间，并支持每秒8000次控制决策。在开放导航基准测试中，锐龙AI嵌入式配置的控制时序可靠性最高达到英伟达Jetson T5000的3.4倍，可用算力余量多1.6倍，同时运行的自主智能体数量最高多2.3倍。
Foundation Robotics与Generative Bionics已采用该方案设计产品。从堆算力跑分到保实时控制，物理AI的竞争规则正在被重新书写。

articles.title: Think Before You Transcribe: Context-Steered Reasoning for Hotword-Aware Speech Recognition
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.26986v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Contextual automatic speech recognition (ASR) improves rare-entity recognition by supplying candidate hotwords, but retrieved candidates may be incomplete or incorrect. A reliable system must therefore exploit a relevant candidate without allowing unsupported alternatives to override the acoustic evidence. We propose a context-steered reasoning framework that generates a short, audio-grounded caption before transcription. This task-specific representation lets the model assess candidate relevance before making a lexical decision. Supervised fine-tuning establishes the structured caption-to-transcription behavior, while targeted trajectory injection strengthens group relative policy optimization when difficult utterances yield only unsuccessful rollouts. Experiments across diverse context conditions show that the proposed method consistently improves both transcription quality and hotword recognition while remaining robust to irrelevant candidates.

articles.title: 英伟达联合思灵推出人形机器人参考平台 Agile ONE SN，计划 2027 年初上市
articles.text:
IT之家 10 月 21 日消息，英伟达当地时间 10 月 21 日在 GTC 柏林大会上宣布扩展 Isaac 开放机器人开发平台，新增人形机器人参考平台、运行框架、仿真资产和数据集，并更新机器人学习工具，覆盖从训练数据生成、仿真训练到实体机器人部署的开发流程。
硬件方面，英伟达联合思灵机器人（Agile Robots）发布了人形机器人参考平台 Agile ONE SN，计划于 2027 年初推出。
该平台预配置英伟达 Isaac GR00T，并搭载 Jetson Thor 计算平台，主要面向机器人研究与开发。通过整合仿真、训练和部署工具，Agile Robots 表示，该平台可将相关环境的前期配置时间从数周缩短至数天。
英伟达创始人兼 CEO 黄仁勋表示，通用机器人技术正在快速发展，机器人领域的“ChatGPT 时刻”正加速到来。英伟达称，此次更新旨在为开发者提供模型、数据、仿真工具和计算系统，帮助他们将通用机器人技术应用于实际产业场景。
思灵机器人 Agile ONE SN 采用 Agile ONE S 人形机器人本体，身高 1.4 米、重量 40 公斤，具有 31 个自由度，单臂负载为 3 公斤。其配备两只 WUJI Hand 2 五指灵巧手，每只手具有 20 个自由度，支持 1kHz 力控制和触觉感知。需要注意的是，路透社报道该机器人重量约为 34 公斤，与英伟达官方公布的 40 公斤数据存在差异，现有信息尚不足以确认差异原因。
计算方面，Agile ONE SN 搭载英伟达 Jetson Thor，提供 2070 TFLOPS 的 FP4 算力和 128GB 统一内存。传感器包括头部及腕部摄像头、激光雷达和惯性测量单元，用于感知周围环境并支持机器人与外部环境交互。
安全方面，该平台计划将机器人端安全协议与英伟达 Halos 全栈安全系统集成，目前这项集成仍待完成。英伟达表示，斯坦福大学、苏黎世联邦理工学院等研究机构已对 Agile ONE SN 表示兴趣。
路透社另报道称，Agile Robots 计划于 2027 年与英伟达合作生产最多 2000 台人形机器人，面向大学和企业研究实验室等客户。
软件方面，英伟达 Isaac Lab 3.0 已正式发布，作为开源机器人学习框架，支持多 GPU 训练工作流，并可使用 Newton、PhysX 等物理引擎。该框架旨在帮助开发者训练和优化机器人策略，覆盖从桌面工作站到数据中心的不同计算环境。
IT之家注意到，英伟达还推出开源运行框架 Isaac OS。该框架基于 Holoscan 构建，用于连接 AI 模型、传感器、控制系统和机器人硬件，支持从仿真环境迁移至实体机器人，并提供确定性实时运行能力。
针对 DGX Station，英伟达同时发布了三套开源参考工作流。第一套通过强化学习优化 GR00T 1.7 模型；第二套利用 Isaac Lab 训练灵巧操作技能；第三套则借助 ChatGPT Astra 对 Cosmos 世界模型进行后训练，以生成合成训练数据。这些工作流旨在帮助开发者整合机器人学习、仿真和数据生成环节。
数据方面，SimReady Central Library 提供超过 2000 项可用于仿真的机器人和工厂资产，涵盖多种机器人设备及工业场景资源。Human 1M 数据集则包含多种人类活动、同步三视角视频和三维手部追踪数据，可用于机器人学习与动作理解。两项资源均通过 Hugging Face 提供，其中完整版本的 Human 1M 数据集仅向 Cosmos Coalition 合作伙伴开放。
英伟达还介绍了多家采用其机器人开发工具的企业。ABB Robotics 将 Omniverse 库整合至 RobotStudio HyperReality，用于机器人系统安装前的仿真和虚拟调试；NEURA Robotics 则利用 Isaac Sim 和 Isaac Lab 生成合成训练数据，并在仿真环境中训练机器人技能。英伟达表示，KUKA、Humanoid、Sereact 和 Universal Robots 等企业也在采用其开放机器人平台相关技术。

articles.title: 黄仁勋投的复旦女学霸，又要融资了！估值冲刺2688亿
articles.text:
智东西
编译 | 黄菲
编辑 | 江宇
智东西10月21日消息，据Business Insider今日报道，AI基础设施初创公司Fireworks AI正就新一轮融资进行初步洽谈，拟以300亿至400亿美元（约合人民币2016亿至2688亿元）的公司估值融资。若最终按这一估值区间完成融资，其公司估值将较今年7月D轮融资时的175亿美元（约合人民币1176亿元）提高约71%至129%。
▲7月公布的融资公告，图源：Fireworks AI
知情人士称，目前融资谈判仍处于早期阶段，最终估值可能发生变化。该公司拒绝置评。
此次融资洽谈发生在该公司10月9日披露安全事件后不久。
在此次安全事件中，入侵者利用内部凭证入侵Fireworks AI，可能导致少量客户API密钥泄露，但该公司已撤销凭证并通知客户，称模型与数据未遭访问。
随着企业对AI模型部署、推理算力和定制化工具的需求增长，Fireworks AI凭借模型推理基础设施实现了快速增长，但该事件也给客户信任带来考验。
一、估值目标最高达2688亿元，英伟达参与D轮投资
Fireworks AI成立于2022年，由7名前Meta工程师和前谷歌工程师共同创立，包括乔琳（Lin Qiao）、本尼·陈（Benny Chen）、赵晨宇（Chenyu Zhao）、德米特罗·朱尔加科夫（Dmytro Dzhulgakov）、德米特罗·伊夫琴科（Dmytro Ivchenko）、詹姆斯·里德（James Reed）和帕维尔·加巴尔茨基（Pawel Garbacki）。
▲Fireworks AI七位联合创始人合照，图源：Fireworks AI
值得一提的是，该公司联合创始人团队中有3位是华人，分别为联合创始人兼首席执行官、前Meta工程高级总监乔琳；前Meta首席软件工程师本尼·陈以及前谷歌高级软件工程师赵晨宇。
其中，乔琳拥有复旦大学计算机科学专业本硕学位，后在美国加州大学圣塔芭芭拉分校取得计算机科学博士学位。
加入Fireworks AI之前，她曾在计算机国际商业公司IBM、职业社交平台领英（LinkedIn）和Meta任职，并在Meta负责PyTorch相关工作。
▲Fireworks AI联合创始人兼首席执行官乔琳，图源：Business Insider
另一位华人联合创始人本尼·陈本科毕业于美国加州大学洛杉矶分校（UCLA），获计算机科学与工程、计算机科学双方向学士学位，GPA高达3.9。
创立Fireworks AI前，本尼·陈与乔琳一样在Meta任职。2014年，他担任Meta的软件工程师；2021年时，本尼·陈成为了该公司的首席软件工程师。
▲本尼·陈履历，图源：领英
赵晨宇本科则毕业于加州大学伯克利分校，拥有电子工程与计算机科学以及工程数学与统计学双学位。他在谷歌任职约9年。
任职期间，他担任该公司的高级资深软件工程师，负责谷歌云Vertex相关业务，是约50人工程师团队的技术经理。
▲赵晨宇履历，图源：领英
今年7月，该公司宣布完成15.05亿美元（约合人民币101.14亿元）D轮融资，估值达到175亿美元（约合人民币1176亿元）。
本轮融资由投资管理公司Atreides Management、风险投资公司Index Ventures、TCV领投，芯片巨头英伟达、风险投资公司Lightspeed Venture Partners、Bessemer Venture Partners、Menlo Ventures等机构参与投资。
在此之前，该公司于2025年10月完成2.5亿美元（约合人民币16.8亿元）C轮融资，估值达到40亿美元（约合人民币269亿元），由风险投资公司Lightspeed Venture Partners、Index Ventures和投资机构Evantic领投。
据The Information于今年9月25日报道，Fireworks AI正考虑以300亿美元（约合人民币2016亿元）的估值寻求新一轮融资。
二、从模型推理到专业化智能，企业需求推动收入增长
Fireworks AI并不以开发面向消费者的通用聊天机器人为主要业务，而是向企业提供AI模型推理基础设施和软件服务，帮助客户运行、微调和部署开源权重模型及定制化AI模型。
该公司将自身的业务方向概括为“专业化智能”（Specialized Intelligence），即结合企业的专有数据、业务流程和具体应用场景，对模型进行定制和优化，使其更好地完成特定任务。
乔琳曾将Fireworks AI比作AI时代的“送水人”。企业无需自行搭建和维护昂贵的算力基础设施，即可通过该平台部署模型，并根据Token使用量付费。
根据Fireworks AI今年7月公布的D轮融资公告，该公司年化营收已超过10亿美元（约合人民币67.2亿元），每日处理的Token超过40万亿个，其中超过95%来自基于客户专有数据定制、针对特定任务优化的模型。
这一业务模式使Fireworks AI能够从企业持续增长的模型调用和定制化需求中获得收入。
三、竞争对手环伺，安全事件考验客户信任
Fireworks AI所处的模型基础设施市场竞争激烈。
竞争对手既包括模型基础设施初创公司Together AI、Baseten和Replicate，也包括云服务巨头亚马逊云、谷歌云、云服务微软Azure以及数据库与云服务巨头甲骨文。
与大型云服务商相比，Fireworks AI专注于模型推理、微调和部署等环节，试图通过优化推理效率、降低使用成本及提供定制化服务吸引企业客户。
不过，随着云服务商不断扩展模型部署和推理服务能力，Fireworks AI这类专业化基础设施企业仍面临竞争压力。
除市场竞争外，近期发生的安全事件也为Fireworks AI带来新的考验。
Fireworks AI于10月9日发布安全公告称，其在10月6日发现内部凭证遭到未经授权使用。
入侵者借此访问了少量客户账户中用于模型评估任务的环境变量，其中包含API密钥和外部服务Token等机密信息。
该公司称，调查尚未发现客户模型、数据集、个人信息或推理流量遭到未经授权访问的证据。
目前，该公司已撤销涉事内部凭证及受影响的API密钥，通知已确认受到影响的客户，并与网络安全专业机构合作调查事件。
10月10日，乔琳在社交平台X上发文称，该公司已控制住事态、撤销相关凭证并通知所有已确认受影响的客户，调查仍在进行。她还承诺，将把这次攻击转化为AI基础设施领域最有力的安全回应。
▲乔琳在社交平台X上发文，图源：X
对于企业AI基础设施提供商而言，客户不仅关注模型成本和部署效率，也关注专有数据及访问凭证是否得到妥善保护。
尽管此次事件中尚未发现客户模型或推理流量遭到访问，环境变量中的凭证被获取，仍意味着相关客户需要检查并轮换受影响的密钥和Token。
结语：估值跃升背后，增长与信任同样重要
Fireworks AI估值快速攀升，反映出资本对AI推理基础设施赛道及企业定制化服务前景的看好。
但在云服务巨头持续加码、同类初创公司竞争加剧的背景下，高估值仍需收入持续增长支撑。
近期安全事件也让客户信任成为其业务扩张必须面对的问题。

articles.title: NVIDIA Confidential Computing Expands, Enabling Frontier Model Builders to Securely Scale Across Global Infrastructure
articles.text:
NVIDIA builds tools to enable safe agents across the stack. The NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture, announced today, is part of NVIDIA’s growing portfolio of technologies that enables organizations to safely deploy agents at scale. NVIDIA Confidential Computing is the infrastructure layer that protects the models and data those agents depend on while running.
Today, NVIDIA is expanding that layer with Confidential Bare Metal, a new deployment option with NVIDIA Confidential Computing that enables frontier model builders to run sensitive workloads on dedicated third-party infrastructure while retaining control of their models and data.
NVIDIA is introducing new platform security controls that protect data in transit, measure platform integrity and enforce hardware-level access restrictions. These new controls let frontier model builders use bare-metal instances to own and operate their bespoke software stack, including host and platform infrastructure software, when operating on NVIDIA accelerated computing infrastructure across third-party cloud, neocloud and enterprise infrastructure.
Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements
NVIDIA Confidential Computing now offers a converged security architecture with three deployment options:
Confidential Bare Metal for bare-metal infrastructure
Confidential Containers for Kubernetes environments
Confidential Virtual Machines for virtualized environments
Organizations can match the right model to their trust boundaries and operating requirements.
NVIDIA Confidential Computing is also expanding across NVIDIA Grace Blackwell and Rubin systems and will integrate with NVIDIA DSX OS as a reference architecture for cloud providers building AI factories.
Model Builders Tap Global Capacity
Confidential Bare Metal gives supported providers a path to serve high-value workloads that require strong model and data privacy protections. For model builders, the expanding ecosystem offers more geographic, sovereign and operational options for scaling training and inference worldwide.
Cohere plans to integrate Confidential Bare Metal into Cohere Model Vault, using NVIDIA Confidential Computing trusted execution environments to extend hardware-rooted security directly to the GPU — protecting models and data in memory and across interconnects during execution.
“Enterprises trust Cohere to provide a secure and confidential platform for inference,” said Phil Blunsom, chief technology officer at Cohere. “With NVIDIA Confidential Computing in Cohere Model Vault, we’re extending hardware-rooted security directly to the GPU, protecting customer data in memory and across interconnects during execution.”
Google Cloud is extending support for  Confidential Bare Metal to A4X Max instances powered by NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems. These will combine non-virtualized NVIDIA accelerated computing with cryptographic protection for training data and model intellectual property.
“Google Cloud introduces Confidential Bare Metal to provide AI labs with hardware-isolated, non-virtualized compute environments and end-to-end cryptographic protection. Our A4X instances, built using NVIDIA Confidential Computing, preserve the privacy of user data, protect model IP, provide top-line serving performance,” said Andrés Lagar-Cavilla, distinguished engineer and AI infrastructure security lead at Google Cloud.
Confidential Computing Expands Across the NVIDIA Platform
NVIDIA Confidential Computing uses hardware-rooted isolation and cryptographic attestation to help protect models and data during execution.
Support now extends to NVIDIA Grace Blackwell NVL72 — bringing Confidential Computing to NVL72 rack-scale systems — as well as x86-based NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 and NVIDIA DGX Rubin NVL8 systems.
CoreWeave, Firmus, GMI Cloud, Google Cloud, IREN, Lambda, Microsoft Azure Infrastructure, Nebius, Nscale and Vultr support NVIDIA Confidential Computing deployments. Global systems partners including Cisco, Dell Technologies, HPE, Lenovo, Supermicro and Bull will support these capabilities with NVIDIA-Certified Systems.
NVIDIA DSX OS will support all NVIDIA Confidential Computing modes, giving cloud providers a software foundation for building and operating AI factories that support confidential workloads.
Learn more about NVIDIA Confidential Computing.

articles.title: Score a 1440p-ready gaming PC with an RTX 5060 Ti 16GB for under $1,500 right now, saving you $200
articles.text:
Right now, the best way to pick up a gaming PC is to buy a pre-built, with hardware prices shooting through the roof. Luckily, the big tech retailers continue to throw out deals for gamers to take advantage of. For instance, you can pick up this ABS Cyclone Aqua machine with an RTX 5060 Ti 16GB GPU, giving you 1440-capable performance for $1,499.99.
● Check out this deal at Newegg
If you took these specs and tried to build a matching PC yourself, you'd struggle to beat this price. Front and center here is the Nvidia GeForce RTX 5060 Ti with 16GB of VRAM: a formidable option for a budget-friendly gaming PC. You're also getting a 20-core Intel Core i7-14700F CPU, 16GB of DDR5 RAM, and a 1TB SSD.
Cyclone Aqua (RTX 5060 Ti 16GB): was $1699.99 now $1499.99
This ABS Cyclone Aqua gaming PC is ready for 1080p and 1440p gaming. It features an Nvidia GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 16GB, 16GB DDR5 RAM, a 1TB SSD, and a 20-core Intel Core i7-14700F CPU.View Deal
With the Nvidia GeForce RTX 5060 Ti at your disposal, you're getting one of Nvidia’s latest-generation mid-tier graphics cards.  It has 4,608 CUDA cores and a boost clock speed of 2,527MHz. Unlike the more power-hungry top-end RTX 50-series cards, you only need one eight-pin PCIe connector to deliver power here, so you can banish those worries about burning GPU cables.
Our RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB review makes clear how good the performance is with this Blackwell GPU for gamers, especially at 1080p and 1440p. The charts you'll see below show that, especially with ray tracing in the mix, compared to rival cards at this level. Full DLSS support is included, too, so you can add multi-frame generation as a backstop. That'll give you a nice frame rate boost in the most resource-heavy games if you're pushing up to the highest resolutions.Tom's HardwareTom's HardwareTom's HardwareTom's Hardware
You can also count on 16GB of GDD7 VRAM with this GPU. That makes it a much more appealing option than 8GB variants you might have to settle for in other rigs at this price point. 16GB gives you more headroom, as far as performance goes, for the most resource-heavy games at 1440p.
For the CPU, you're getting the Intel Core i7-14700F. This continues to be a popular CPU option for gaming, despite being a little older. This Raptor Lake Refresh CPU has 20 cores, with eight performance cores, which are the ones you'll want for gaming, along with 12 efficient cores for multi-threaded work. It also has a maximum turbo clock speed of 5.4 GHz, along with a 65W TDP. At 1080p or 1440p, you won't see much of a bottleneck with the 14700F at your disposal in modern games.
No risk of settling for slower DDR4 RAM here, either. You get fast DDR5 instead, with 16GB of G.Skill Flare X5 DDR5 memory included with speeds of 6,000 MT/s. You aren't getting 32GB, which is a compromise, but you do have room to upgrade later, and DDR5 ensures some extra longevity.
Storage-wise, you're also getting a 1TB Patriot P410 SSD. It has Gen 4 speeds, with that 1TB of storage ensuring you get space for a couple of the big AAA games alongside your Windows installation. This ABS build also comes with Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.2 wireless connectivity, along with gigabit Ethernet for a wired connection to your local network.
The $1,499.99 sale price for this ABS Cyclone Aqua gaming PC makes it an affordable option for gamers who want a 1440p-ready rig right now, especially with prices rising elsewhere. The RTX 5060 Ti 16GB is the standout component, but there's no guarantee that this price will last for very long.
